messages:
sam: Heads-up — Acme POC can't reach Dedicated UI and their Hosted API key wasn't auto-provisioned. They can SSO in, but no dedicated roles show. Looks like groups aren't landing via SCIM. Anyone seen this exact mismatch?

maria: Which tenant + user? Is this Okta SAML + SCIM group push or just SAML group claims?

sam: tenant=acme-tenant-42, user=jane@acme.com. They use Okta app (RDW-PROD). Okta shows the user in 'rdw-dedicated_admin' group but inside our console the user is not in that group. Hosted API key auto-provision expects membership in that group to create the key.

kevin: Common cause: Okta group push wasn't enabled or the Group Push filter didn't include the group name. Also sometimes Okta pushes groups but the SCIM payload omits members due to permission mapping. Quick check — can you run this?

kevin: ```bash
curl -s -u $SCIM_TOKEN: "https://scim.redwood.com/v2/Users?filter=emails.value%20eq%20%22jane@acme.com%22" | jq '.Resources[0]'
```

kevin: Look for "groups" or "memberships" fields in the returned resource. If groups are missing, SCIM push not including group membership.

lee-idp: Also verify the SAML assertion mapping for groups. If you rely on SCIM for canonical groups, SAML claim absence is OK, but if your Okta app is configured to send group claims instead of pushing groups, we won't see them via SCIM.

maria: Another gotcha: Okta "Push Groups" can be configured to push only groups assigned to the app or groups matching a filter (startsWith / contains). If the customer's group is nested or has a trailing space/UTF char we fail the match. Ask them to try a manual group push from the Okta app > Push Groups UI and watch the Provisioning logs.

okta-bot: Provisioning event: 2024-08-21T15:02:11Z GRP_PUSH: app=RDW-PROD group=rdw-dedicated_admin status=200 member_count=1

nora-cs: We looked at their Okta logs — group push succeeded but our SCIM logs show a PUT /Groups/{gid} with body missing "members" array. That explains it: group exists in RDW but no members attached. Need either Okta to include members on push or we backfill via /Users membership check.

kevin: Short-term workaround if customer needs access now: we can create a tenant role mapping entry for jane@acme.com (manual user member) or create an API key for them. To create API key as admin: 

kevin: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/admin/tenants/acme-tenant-42/api-keys" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"label":"acme-poc-temp","scopes":["dedicated:admin"],"user_email":"jane@acme.com"}'
```

maria: We'll need an approval email from Acme to create keys for them — security requirement. If they approve, we can generate a time-limited key and tag it as manual workaround.

sam: I'll ask them for written approval. In parallel can someone walk their Okta admin through the Push Groups flow? They said they "enabled provisioning" but might not have checked member sync.

lee-idp: Steps for their Okta admin: App > Provisioning > Edit > Enable Group Push. Then App > Assignments > Push Groups > Select rdw-* group > Push. Also ensure SCIM scope on the Okta service account includes Group.ReadWrite and GroupMember.ReadWrite.

kevin: If they prefer SAML group claims instead, set the app to include a Groups claim in the assertion (filter to only rdw-* groups). We have a mapping that will translate SAML groups to our tenant roles if the claim name is "groups" and values are the group names. (But note: group claim length limits sometimes push Okta to send group by reference instead of full list.)

nora-cs: After they pushed, I saw a retry. okta-bot: Provisioning event: 2024-08-21T15:07:02Z GRP_PUSH: app=RDW-PROD group=rdw-dedicated_admin status=200 member_count=1 payload_members=1

kevin: Confirmed on our side — group now shows members in SCIM and jane@acme.com receives Dedicated access. Hosted API key auto-provisioner also kicked in and created a temp key (label acme-poc-temp-1) — please confirm with client and rotate/remove after POC.

sam: Thanks all. I'll get the approval email, confirm they pushed groups, and follow up once they validate API key works in their app. :thumbsup:

maria: Added a short KB for the customer (link): https://redwood.internal/kb/okta-scim-group-push-guide (shared).

sam: closing loop — Acme confirms Dedicated UI + API key worked. We'll document for future POCs to check Group Push + SCIM member sync first.
